shortDefinition: The coordination and management of multiple AI agents, tools, and services to execute complex workflows.
fullDefinition: Orchestration is the process of coordinating multiple AI components — agents, tools, models, and services — to execute complex, multi-step workflows. An orchestrator manages the sequence of operations, handles dependencies between steps, routes data between components, and ensures the overall process achieves its goals. In AI systems, orchestration frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, and AutoGen provide primitives for defining agent roles, managing conversation flows, and handling error recovery. Good orchestration makes complex AI systems feel like single, coherent applications to end users, hiding the complexity of the underlying components.
examples: Orchestrating a research pipeline: search, read, summarize, and format
Coordinating a customer support workflow: classify, search KB, draft response, escalate
Managing a code review pipeline: lint, test, analyze, and report findings
